articles.title: Four people, including a child, killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza
articles.summary: Gaza officials say more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the so-called ‘ceasefire’ took effect.
articles.body:
Israeli attacks have killed at least four Palestinians, including a child, in central and southern Gaza, medical sources say, as Israeli forces keep up near-daily strikes in the enclave.

Medical sources at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir el-Balah said Abdul Rahim Walid Matar, 27, was killed at dawn on Thursday when an Israeli drone fired two missiles at a tent sheltering displaced people west of az-Zawayda.

Nasser Medical Complex said a woman was killed and two people were wounded by Israeli fire outside areas under Israeli military control in Khan Younis. A source at al-Awda Hospital said a child was killed by Israeli fire in Bureij refugee camp.

Reporting from Deir el-Balah, Al Jazeera’s Ashraf Amra said Israeli forces opened direct fire on homes and tents in eastern Bureij, killing the child on the spot.

“Israeli forces on the edges of the area that directly overlooks al-Mawasi are firing heavily towards the tents of displaced people,” Amra said. He added that a man sitting inside his tent was critically wounded and taken into surgery at Nasser.

Another drone strike at Az-zawaya killed another person, medical sources told Al Jazeera, bringing the death toll to four.

An Israeli drone also struck a gathering of residents in the al-Baraka area of Deir el-Balah, wounding several people, one critically.

In the north, a source at al-Shifa Hospital told Al Jazeera a Palestinian was wounded when a drone struck an apartment in al-Karama, northwest of Gaza City. Israeli artillery shelled eastern Gaza City heavily, and naval vessels fired towards the coastline.

Local sources said Israeli military vehicles fired heavily around the Hosni al-Musaddar Mosque east of Maghazi camp, and a drone dropped a bomb nearby. No injuries were reported there. Residents east of Khan Younis reported two powerful explosions as the army blew up homes and civilian facilities inside areas it controls.

Amra said Israeli forces were also pushing forward on the eastern edges of al-Musaddar and Deir el-Balah, bulldozing homes and farmland and absorbing more land behind the so-called “Yellow Line”.

On Wednesday, Gaza’s Health Ministry reported three Palestinians had been killed and 21 wounded in the previous 24 hours. One of the three had died of earlier wounds.

The ministry says 1,602 Palestinians have been killed and 5,794 wounded since the ceasefire took effect on October 11, 2025. These deaths put the overall toll since October 2023 at 74,618 killed and 175,920 wounded.

Gaza’s Government Media Office said on Monday that Israel had committed 5,989 ceasefire violations since the truce began . Of those, 753 came in October; among them 346 shootings, 310 bombardments and 64 home demolitions.

articles.title: Southport and Nottingham attack victims call out NHS snooping
articles.summary: Families described the unauthorised access of confidential medical records as an "abuse of power".
articles.body:
Families affected by the Southport and Nottingham attacks have called for stronger safeguards against NHS staff improperly accessing confidential patient records.

In an open letter, they described the breaches as a "flagrant abuse of power" and urged ministers and NHS leaders to take further action.

More than 30 people have signed the letter, including those affected by the maternity scandals.

The BBC has contacted NHS England, the Department for Health and Social Care and Department for Culture for comment.

Grace O'Malley-Kumar, Barnaby Webber, both 19, and grandfather Ian Coates, 65, were stabbed to death in the street by Valdo Calocane in Nottingham in 2023.

The authors of the letter highlighted how, in the wake of the attack, "staff began prying, while parents were still coming to terms with the deaths of their children. Other victims were still in hospital fighting for their lives when their records were breached".

NHS workers also snooped on the records of victims of the Southport attack, when Axel Rudakubana killed Bebe King, six, Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven, and nine-year-old Alice Da Silva Aguiar during a Taylor Swift-themed dance class in 2024.

"Strangers, who had no direct involvement in their care, probed their most sensitive and personal information in a flagrant abuse of power," the authors wrote.

This "deeply troubling" behaviour has been repeated following other high profile incidents, they said.

Liverpool Heart and Chest NHS Foundation Trust is investigating allegations staff inappropriately accessed Southport stabbing victims' medical records.

In May, the University Hospitals of Liverpool Group (UHLG) admitted that nearly 50 of its staff had wrongly looked at victims' medical files and there is a separate investigation being held at North West Ambulance Service Trust in relation to staff looking up the victims of the attack without authorisation.

The authors said the issue was "not exclusive to the NHS" as they highlighted how the Ministry of Justice and HM Courts and Tribunals Service "have both apologised for inappropriate access of sensitive, personal information belonging to the Southport victims".

In September NHS officials announced a crackdown on staff inappropriately accessing patient medical records.

Health chiefs said that staff suspected of snooping will be suspended immediately and have their access to health service computer systems cut off.

But the measures do not go far enough to prevent such behaviour in the future, according to the letter.

The authors have called for a "tick box" to enable staff to access records which confirms they have legitimate reason to do so.

They have also called for audits on snooping and for patients to be "properly recognised" by the Information Commissioner.

"These breaches are deeply distressing and entirely preventable," the authors said.

"We believe these three measures would make significant progress in tackling the problem and preventing further harm."

Nicola Ryan-Donnelly, partner at Fletchers Solicitors which penned the letter, said: "We have written and published this open letter because victims of NHS snooping have had enough.

"Every week in the media we are learning of a new breach into patient's medical records by staff who have no legitimate cause to access them.

"Among the child Southport survivors I represent, many of their parents do not feel they have a voice to speak out about how this has affected them.

"They had hoped that their anonymity would protect their children's most vulnerable and difficult moments, but the truth is staff have repeatedly abused their position to pry into their most private and sensitive information.

"Anybody, no matter who they are or what they have been through, should feel confident and that staff will protect their privacy and dignity while they are being treated or cared for by the NHS and other agencies.

"Stronger sanctions and dismissals for NHS staff who snoop is a step in the right direction, but it does not do enough to address the problem.

"We have to instil a new culture in our health system and give victims a powerful voice to challenge breaches."

articles.summary: Alta Pierson competed in the Huntsman World Senior Games and won hearts on social media when a video of her running went viral. The centenarian’s tips for a long life.
articles.body: Alta Pierson had to move some things around for this interview. The 101-year-old’s schedule is bursting with lunch plans with friends, church events, volunteering, library trips and baking for the many fans of her homemade bread. Most recently, however, Pierson was booked and busy adding world records to her list of feats. In October, just weeks before her 101st birthday, she competed in the Huntsman World Senior Games. Making her track meet debut, Pierson ran the 50-meter race in a cool 1:01:61. Naturally, this kind of speed earned her the record at the games in the 100–104-year-old division. And it’s not her only one. Spectators didn’t know it as they were crowding the stands that day in St. George, Utah, but they were in for a four-peat performance from Pierson, too. That day, she also took home gold for edging out her opponents in the shot put and 400-meter run, and the discus and javelin, for which she also won the world records respectively. It’s a demanding life for a champion, but Pierson’s up for the challenge. She shared her tips for a long and healthy life with TODAY.com. Love What You Do For years, Pierson worked as a high school home economics teacher. She went on to work at a library, then at universities in Nevada and Utah, before she returned to teaching home ec in her hometown of St. George, where she remains today. “It’s been a wonderful career for me,” Pierson says about her experience teaching home economics. “I loved being with the girls. They were just so much fun,” she tells TODAY.com. “They were really receptive to the things (I taught). So, it was a wonderful experience.” When Pierson ran into one of her former students, the student admitted she’d always wished she’d had Pierson by her side when she went off to college. Keep Loved Ones Close Pierson grew up with six sisters and two brothers. She was married twice, first to a doctor and later to a forest ranger, and she’s a mother to five daughters and one son. Her family tree is dwindling, she says. Her parents, siblings, both husbands and three of her children have died. Yet love and loved ones remain a constant in her life. Pierson lives just “around the corner” from her daughter, Demaree Johnson, whom she sees regularly. She lives with her granddaughter. Her daughter-in-law and three grandchildren were visiting Pierson at the time of this interview. Outside of family, Pierson shops, spends time with and takes walks with her friends from church and her neighborhood. Be Open to Trying Saying yes just might earn you a world record or two. Pierson was reluctant to compete in the 2026 Senior Games at first. “Demaree’s husband was the conceiver of the idea,” she says. He’d been competing in the Games for several years and was adamant that Pierson would land herself on the winner’s podium since there were so few 100-year-old competitors. When she brushed off the idea, he wooed her, gifting her a javelin and a discus last Christmas. Soon enough, they were training. “We practiced quite a bit,” says Pierson. But on the day of the competition, “I didn’t throw as far as I wanted,” she said about her discus performance. Still, she earned herself the world record. And she also nabbed the world record for the shot put. By the end of the Games, Pierson had earned gold for her performances in the javelin competition, and 50-meter and 400-meter races, too. For anyone hesitant about going after a daunting goal, Pierson says, “Go for it. ... It was kind of nerve-wracking to be out there, trying to do something with people watching.” But, she adds, it was worth it. Stay Active — Both Mentally and Physically Pierson doesn’t call herself an athlete, but she’s always been active. She was an avid swimmer until she was 98. She’s since slowed down a bit, though. Now, aside from her showings at the Games, she’s focused on getting her steps in. Her favorite form of movement is walking, especially making loops around the local mall with friends. Occupy Your Mind and Hands Pierson’s known for her baking. She’s always baked bread, but cinnamon rolls are her specialty. Once she’s shared her baked goods with family and friends, she turns her attention to books, making frequent trips to the library. She’s also got a gift for sewing. “I did nearly all the clothes that I had,” says Pierson, and she made clothing for all of her children. When she wasn’t working on clothing, she’d hand-make quilts — something she still does for her great-grandchildren. These days, she also sews for an organization that supports girls worldwide who have limited access to menstrual products and education. Look After Your Health If you live to be 100 or older, suddenly everyone will start asking you for the secret to a long life, and Pierson hates the question. She answers it anyway: “Well, just try to take care of (yourself) and get up every morning.” Pierson has never smoked, doesn’t drink and eats meals made from whole foods, including a lot of fruit. Her genes, she and her daughter agree, likely have something to do with it, too.

articles.title: British doctor infected with Ebola in DR Congo being treated at London hospital
articles.summary: The doctor tested positive in DR Congo, where there is an outbreak. The government says the risk to the public remains low.
articles.body:
A British doctor who tested positive for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been flown back to the UK.

The man, who has not been identified, landed at RAF Northolt before being transported to a specialist infectious diseases unit at the Royal Free Hospital in north London.

It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths.

Dr Renu Bindra, deputy director of the All Hazards Public Health Response team at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), said there are "well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this" and the risk to the public remains low.

What is Ebola and why is stopping the latest outbreak so difficult?

The infected doctor was brought to the UK on a medical evacuation flight as part of a joint effort by the UK and DR Congo governments and their international health partners, the Department of Health (DoH) said.

A convoy of emergency vehicles were on hand to complete the transfer following the man's arrival at the RAF base.

Three large police vans travelled at either end of the convey, while two ambulances and another support car were involved.

Traffic was stopped and police exited the vans to keep the public away as the convey arrived at the Royal Free Hospital.

The man is now being treated in a "highly specialised" isolation unit at the hospital, the DoH said.

The Royal Free Hospital successfully treated three health workers who had been evacuated after the Ebola outbreak in West Africa in 2014 and 2015.

There have only been four confirmed cases of the virus in the UK - one, in 1976, resulting from a laboratory incident, and three involving health workers who were responding to an outbreak in West Africa between 2014 and 2015.

None of these cases have resulted in a death.

There have been more than 10,000 confirmed cases since the recent outbreak in DR Congo started in May, which has grown to become the second most deadly recorded spate of infections, behind the outbreak in West Africa in the 2010s.

The current outbreak in DR Congo has a fatality rate of 48.6% reported at the end of last month.

Ebola can result in serious illness and death. Early symptoms include vomiting and diarrhoea but it can progress to organ failure and internal bleeding.

The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

The ongoing outbreak centred on DR Congo is fuelled by the Bundibugyo variant of the virus.

There is no approved vaccine but the World Health Organization said experts have recommended adding two new candidate drugs to an ongoing clinical trial.

The vaccines, one developed by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, and another by the firm Moderna, will join the trial once they are approved by Congolese health authorities.

It will be the first time jabs specifically designed to protect against the Bundibugyo virus are tested during an outbreak.

Since the outbreak, Ebola cases have also been confirmed in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda.

articles.title: Wisconsin reports its first measles death in decades, the third in the U.S. this week
articles.summary: The infant’s death followed a measles-associated death reported Wednesday in Pennsylvania and another Monday in New York.
articles.body: An infant in Wisconsin has died of measles, the state health department said Thursday — the third measles-related death reported in the U.S. this week. It’s Wisconsin’s first measles-related death since 1990, the Health Service Department said, adding that a coroner had listed measles as the infant’s immediate cause of death. The news came just one day after Pennsylvania’s Health Department reported another measles-associated death there — the state’s sixth this year. It said Wednesday that an unvaccinated resident in Jefferson County who tested positive for measles had died. On Monday, New York health officials announced that a child in Lewis County had died of measles. Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency over measles in early October. In total, the U.S. has recorded eight measles-associated deaths this year, according to state health department data. It’s the highest measles death toll in the country since 1991. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed four of those deaths. It says it will update its count “as additional information becomes available and relevant reviews are completed.” None of the eight people who have died were vaccinated, according to state health departments; some were ineligible because of their age or health status. Typically, the first dose of the vaccine is administered around a child’s first birthday. Before the outbreaks in Wisconsin, New York and Pennsylvania, none of the states had recorded a measles death in more than 30 years. Dr. Stephanie Schauer, the immunization program director at the Wisconsin health department, said some chains of transmission started with residents traveling out of state to events like funerals and weddings. The department is recommending an early dose of the measles vaccine for infants as young as 6 months who are at increased risk of exposure. Around 500 such early doses have been administered since August, Schauer said. Around 85% of kindergartners in Wisconsin have been vaccinated against measles — below the national average of 92%. Experts say 95% is the threshold needed to keep the population protected. “We can actually eliminate transmission of measles in the community by getting enough people vaccinated,” said Dr. Ryan Westergaard, the state epidemiologist for communicable diseases. “We have the opportunity to take a disease that could affect everybody and essentially make it go away.” The health department said it has sent out 2,000 additional measles vaccine doses to local health departments over the last few months. Nationally, the CDC has confirmed 4,852 measles cases this year — more than double last year’s count and the most since 1991. The dramatic rise is linked, in part, to a decline in vaccination rates across the country. Two doses of the measles vaccine are 97% effective against the disease. Pennsylvania’s outbreak, which began in April, is by far the largest in the country, with a case total approaching 1,500 across 45 counties, according to the state Health Department. A Franklin County coroner reported an additional death last month possibly linked to measles, but the state Health Department said Wednesday that it has not yet confirmed any deaths as measles-associated in the county. Measles has been considered eliminated in the U.S. since 2000, a designation that indicates the virus is no longer constantly circulating, though there can be occasional outbreaks. The Pan American Health Organization, a group within the World Health Organization, will meet next week to determine whether the U.S. should lose its elimination status. Measles infections are particularly dangerous for babies and young children, whose immune systems aren’t always developed enough to fight an infection. Roughly 1 to 3 out of every 1,000 children with measles die from respiratory and neurological complications, according to the CDC. Measles often starts with a high fever, cough, runny nose and pink or watery eyes. From there, people may develop white spots on the insides of the cheeks near the molars and a blotchy rash of flat, red spots. Severe cases can progress to pneumonia or swelling of the brain.

articles.title: Popular weight-loss drugs may prevent prediabetes from turning into diabetes
articles.summary: A large study found GLP-1 medications like semaglutide and tirzepatide are linked to 41% lower all-cause mortality risk versus metformin in prediabetes.
articles.body: Adults with prediabetes and obesity who took GLP-1-based medications had a 31% lower risk of developing type 2 diabetes and a 41% lower risk of death compared with those taking metformin. Metformin is an oral medication used primarily to treat type 2 diabetes, widely considered the first-line treatment, combined with lifestyle modifications. It is also sometimes prescribed to people with prediabetes to help prevent or delay progression. The findings, which come from a large observational study, are set to be presented at the American Heart Association’s Scientific Sessions 2026 this weekend in Chicago. They have not yet undergone the full peer review process. DR OZ LINKS OBESITY TO CHRONIC DISEASE SURGE, SAYS GLP-1S CAN 'JUMPSTART' BETTER HEALTH The study involved health records for 256,492 adults with prediabetes and obesity, averaging 52 years of age. Approximately half of the group received GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists) medications – including semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide and dulaglutide – and half received metformin. Based on a three-year follow-up, in addition to the lower risk of diabetes and all-cause mortality, GLP-1–based medications were associated with 20% fewer strokes, 15% fewer heart attacks and 25% fewer cases of heart failure. "The 41% lower risk of death from any cause surprised me most," study author Vinicius de Sousa Barzon Serra, M.D., a research fellow in the department of cardiovascular medicine at the Mayo Clinic in Scottsdale, Arizona, told Fox News Digital. "I expected GLP-1 medications to do better than metformin on blood sugar and diabetes risk, because they lead to much more weight loss. I was also struck that the benefit appeared across many outcomes, including heart attack, stroke, heart failure and atrial fibrillation." POPULAR DIET SLASHES LIVER FAT BY 67% WHILE REVERSING PREDIABETES IN SOME PEOPLE Nearly 40% of U.S. adults have prediabetes, according to statistics from the AHA. That condition is marked by blood sugar levels that are above normal but not yet elevated enough for a diabetes diagnosis. As many as 10% of those with prediabetes will go on to develop type 2 diabetes each year. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES "Most earlier research on these medications focused on people who already had diabetes," Serra noted. "Our study suggests the prediabetes stage may be an important time to consider them, rather than waiting until they develop type 2 diabetes." The study did have some limitations. While it found a link between GLP-1 medications and better health outcomes, it does not prove that the drugs were responsible. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER The findings are preliminary until published in a peer-reviewed journal, Serra noted. "We matched patients by age, health conditions and other characteristics to make the groups comparable … even so, other differences between the groups may remain," he said. "We also grouped the GLP-1 medications together, so we could not tell whether individual drugs differ." The study relied on patients' electronic health records, which may have contained missing or incorrect information. It is also possible that factors not measured in the study, such as medication dosage and compliance, could have influenced the results, the researchers noted. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ People with prediabetes and obesity should talk with their doctor about all their options and should not stop or change any medication on their own, Serra advised. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Metformin is a safe, inexpensive option with a long track record, and lifestyle changes such as healthy eating, regular physical activity and weight management remain the foundation of treatment," he emphasized to Fox News Digital. "For some patients, a GLP-1 medication may be worth discussing, depending on their overall health, other medical conditions, cost and access. The decision should be made together with their doctor."

articles.title: NBC’s Chloe Melas Opens Up About Parenting With Chronic Illness in Exclusive Book Excerpt
articles.summary: Chloe Melas, NBC News entertainment correspondent, has been living with a type of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) called ulcerative colitis (UC) for 15 years.
articles.body: Chloe Melas, NBC News entertainment correspondent, has been living with a type of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) called ulcerative colitis (UC) for 15 years. UC causes sores in the colon, leading to diarrhea, bloody stool, pain and cramping, urgency to pass stool, and more. Over the years, Melas has endured surgeries, hospitalizations and countless colonoscopies due to her chronic illness. In her new book, “The Girl’s Guide to Guts: Everything Your Doc Didn’t Tell You (But Your Bestie Would),” she and co-author Judy Batalion, who also has UC, offer honest advice about how to navigate these challenging symptoms when life gets busy due to work, kids, dating and beyond. Melas shared an exclusive excerpt from the book, out Nov. 10, with TODAY.com. Read an Excerpt From ‘The Girl’s Guide to Guts’ by Chloe Melas and Judy Batalion Getting pregnant and giving birth can be challenging, but so can taking care of those children (or others) when you are ill. Living with ulcerative colitis as a parent is a little like trying to pitch a tent in the middle of a tornado. The odds are pretty much stacked against you. Most days, I think I do a pretty good job of putting on a brave face. Mornings are dedicated to making sure the kids’ lunches are ready, their homework is done, and reminding them for the fourth time to brush their teeth — all while I’m checking countless emails and trying to make my train to Manhattan. On the outside, it probably looks like any other family. On the inside, I’m thinking: I haven’t had a bowel movement yet ... should I drink that second cup of coffee? Do I feel a twinge of pain in my lower left abdominal? IBD is a thief in many ways. It steals moments. It steals time. It takes up mental and emotional space that I wish I was channeling towards my loved ones. I’ve missed parts of my kids’ sports games because I couldn’t be too far from home. I’ve cut an errand so close that I raced home, desperately hoping I wouldn’t get pulled over for going above the speed limit just so that I could make it to the bathroom. And then there are the warm baths in the middle of a Saturday afternoon. To me, they’re relief. A reset. A way to calm inflammation in my body and just breathe for a minute. But I sometimes wonder if the kids are going to remember that I was in the bathroom ... a lot. The hardest part isn’t even the day-to-day discomfort. It’s the mom guilt. What I’m learning is that parenting with a chronic illness forces you to redefine what “showing up” looks like and learn how to give myself some grace. My boys may not understand it now, but one day I hope they know that even on the days when my body makes things really freaking hard, my heart never stops loving them and my mind never stops thinking about them. I’m still there for the bedtime stories, the hugs, the late-night cases of the giggles, and the million questions about megalodons. IBD may have its rainy-ass days, but it’s not going to win, because I’m not going to let it. In some ways, I think I may even be a better version of myself because of the hard times, and I hope to pass my resilience on to Leo and Luke. Chloe’s Tips for Being a Mother During a Chronic Illness Flare 1. Ask for help. Whether it’s a family member, babysitter, or friend, be honest that you need some support. When weekends roll around, they are often jam-packed with sports, and sometimes I’m stuck in the bathroom with mere minutes to spare before I run the risk of my sons being late to their practices or games. That’s when my mom tribe becomes so essential. Shout-out to Sara, Alicia, Paula, Jackie, and Jessyka, who have handled countless drop-offs and pickups when I’ve been indisposed. 2. Keep your routine. Take your medicine, stool softeners, and any supplements at the same time every day. I’ve found that my routine, including drinking my morning coffee and eating my Greek yogurt for breakfast, has to be within a certain window or it throws my body off. 3. Have an exit strategy. Is it weird that I’ve dreamed of a car where the seat can turn into an actual toilet? Yes, this is an actual thought of mine when it comes to long car rides. Whether it’s the soccer field, gymnasium, or spring break trip, look for the nearest restroom and bring a change of underwear.

articles.title: Mulher grávida morre e outra fica ferida após serem baleadas na Bahia | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso aconteceu no bairro da Liberdade, nesta sexta-feira (6). Segunda mulher foi baleada na perna e levada para o Hospital Geral do Estado (HGE).
articles.summary: Caso aconteceu no bairro da Liberdade, nesta sexta-feira (6). Segunda mulher foi baleada na perna e levada para o Hospital Geral do Estado (HGE).
articles.body:
DHPP investiga crime Polícia Civil da Bahia — Foto: Divulgação/Polícia Civil da Bahia

Uma mulher, grávida de seis meses, morreu e outra ficou ferida após serem baleadas nesta sexta-feira (6), em uma rua do bairro da Liberdade, em Salvador .

Segundo apuração da equipe de reportagem da TV Bahia, a mulher foi identificada inicialmente apenas como Vanessa. Um homem que passava caminhando pelo local atirou contra Vanessa e os disparos acabaram atingindo outra mulher que passava pelo local.

Equipes do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foram acionadas, mas, ao chegarem ao local, constataram que ela já estava morta. A vítima deixa quatro filhos.

A segunda mulher foi atingida por um tiro na perna. Ela foi socorrida e encaminhada para o Hospital Geral do Estado (HGE). Não há informações sobre o estado de saúde dela.

Policiais militares da 37ª Companhia Independente da Polícia Militar (CIPM) foram acionados e realizaram diligências na região para tentar localizar os responsáveis pelos disparos.

Em nota, a Polícia Civil informou que o Departamento de Homicídios e Proteção à Pessoa (DHPP) investiga o caso. A corporação destacou que a vítima ainda não foi identificada formalmente.

O Departamento de Polícia Técnica (DPT) foi acionado para realizar perícia e encaminhar o corpo para o Instituto Médico Legal (IML).

A polícia realiza oitivas e outras diligências para identificar a autoria e esclarecer a motivação do crime. Até a última atualização desta reportagem, ninguém havia sido preso.

articles.title: Doação de órgãos de goleiro de 14 anos salva quatro vidas em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Transplantes de coração, fígado e rins foram realizados após a captação dos órgãos de Miguel Meneses, em 29 de outubro, segundo a Secretaria de Estado da Saúde.
articles.summary: A doação de órgãos de Miguel Meneses, goleiro de 14 anos do São José, salvou quatro vidas com transplantes de coração, fígado e rins após acidente no interior de SP.
articles.body:
Quatro pessoas foram beneficiadas com os transplantes de órgãos do goleiro Miguel Meneses, de 14 anos, que morreu após um acidente de trânsito em São José dos Campos (SP) . A informação foi confirmada ao g1 pela Secretaria de Estado da Saúde de São Paulo (SES-SP).

Segundo a pasta, a captação dos órgãos do adolescente foi concluída no dia 29 de outubro. Ao todo, foram realizados transplantes de coração, fígado e rins. A Secretaria informou que todos os procedimentos previstos foram concluídos com sucesso.

A família de Miguel autorizou a doação dos órgãos após a confirmação da morte encefálica do adolescente. O procedimento de captação começou por volta das 22h do dia 28 de outubro e terminou durante a madrugada do dia seguinte, no Hospital Municipal de São José dos Campos .

O coração era considerado o órgão prioritário, já que precisa ser transplantado em um período de até quatro horas após a retirada. Também foram captados o fígado, os rins e as córneas, conforme as informações divulgadas pelo hospital na ocasião.

Goleiro Miguel Meneses, do sub-15 São José. — Foto: Reprodução/Assessoria do SJEC

Miguel morreu na noite de terça-feira (27), após ficar internado na Unidade de Terapia Intensiva (UTI) do Hospital Municipal. Ele havia sido vítima de um acidente de trânsito no domingo (25), no Anel Viário, na região do bairro Monte Castelo, em São José dos Campos.

O carro em que o adolescente estava com familiares perdeu o controle em uma curva e bateu contra uma árvore. O acidente aconteceu durante a chuva e deixou quatro familiares gravemente feridos.

Após a confirmação da morte encefálica, a família autorizou a doação dos órgãos. A decisão foi uma forma encontrada pelos parentes para transformar a perda em uma oportunidade de ajudar outras pessoas que aguardavam por transplantes.

Na ocasião, o irmão do adolescente, Benício Meneses, f alou sobre a importância da decisão para a família.

“A gente viu que os órgãos dele podem ajudar a salvar outras vidas, como vai ajudar. A gente tem certeza disso”, afirmou.

Antes da cirurgia de captação, profissionais do Hospital Municipal fizeram um corredor de aplausos para homenagear Miguel . A passagem pelo corredor marcou a despedida do adolescente antes do procedimento.

Miguel era goleiro da equipe sub-15 do São José Esporte Clube desde 2025. A morte do adolescente provocou comoção entre familiares, amigos, colegas de equipe e integrantes do clube.

Durante a internação, jogadores e familiares receberam manifestações de apoio. Atletas da equipe sub-17 do São José também prestaram homenagem ao colega ao entrar em campo com uma faixa antes de uma partida contra o Corinthians, pelo Campeonato Paulista.

O adolescente foi velado na Câmara Municipal de São José dos Campos e sepultado no Memorial do Vale, em Jacare í. Durante a despedida, as luvas de goleiro foram colocadas junto ao caixão, em uma homenagem à paixão de Miguel pelo futebol.

articles.summary: Vítimas foram arremessadas da cabine após acidente, entre as cidades de Maracás e Jequié. Casal morava em Feira de Santana e deixa dois filhos
articles.body:
Mutirão de combate ao câncer de próstata oferece 500 vagas para consultas e exames — Foto: Divulgação/Sesab

Um mutirão de combate ao câncer de próstata irá oferecer 500 vagas para consultas com urologista e exames de PSA, em Salvador , no dia 14 de novembro.

A informação foi divulgada pela Secretaria da Saúde da Bahia (Sesab) nesta sexta-feira (6). As vagas são limitadas e o atendimento só será realizado mediante agendamento prévio.

As inscrições poderão ser feitas pela internet, no site da pasta , a partir da segunda (9). A ação acontecerá no Hospital Geral Roberto Santos (HGRS), no bairro do Cabula.

Durante a ação serão atendidos homens cis, mulheres trans e pessoas não binárias a partir dos 40 anos. Além da prevenção, o objetivo é ter a detecção precoce do câncer de próstata.

articles.title: Falta de autorização para médicos gera atrasos no HGR e Cosme e Silva | G1
articles.standfirst: Pacientes enfrentaram horas de espera na manhã desta sexta-feira (6). Governo não emitiu Ordem de Serviço para empresas que fornecem profissionais da saúde para plantões. Sesau nega.
articles.summary: Pacientes enfrentaram horas de espera na manhã desta sexta-feira (6). Governo não emitiu Ordem de Serviço para empresas que fornecem profissionais da saúde para plantões.
articles.body:
Pacientes aguardam no Pronto Atendimento Cosme e Silva, no bairro Pintolândia, Zona Oeste de Boa Vista. — Foto: Vinícius Picanço/Rede Amazônica

Pacientes relataram horas de espera por atendimento no Hospital Geral de Roraima (HGR) e no Pronto Atendimento Cosme e Silva , em Boa Vista , na manhã desta sexta-feira (6). O g1 apurou que a demora ocorreu porque médicos que prestam serviço para a rede estadual ficaram impedidos de assumir os plantões , devido à falta de Ordem de Serviço que deveria ser emitida pelo governo .

Entenda 🔎: Sem a Ordem de Serviço , a atuação dos médicos nas unidades de saúde é considerada ilegal. Profissionais que não quiseram se identificar relataram que as empresas pelas quais são contratados estavam há cinco dias sem o documento oficial para exercer as funções nos plantões.

Procurada, a Secretaria de Estado da Saúde (Sesau) não falou sobre o motivo para a demora nos atendimentos, mas negou que o Hospital Cosme e Silva esteja sem ordem de serviço. Em nota, a pasta informou que "a situação está regularizada e os serviços seguem normalmente" .

Sem os profissionais suficientes, os pacientes enfrentaram horas de espera . Um homem que buscou atendimento para a esposa no Cosme e Silva na manhã desta sexta, e preferiu não se identificar, relatou à Rede Amazônica as dificuldades na unidade.

Ele contou que, com a falta de equipe, os próprios acompanhantes precisavam buscar cadeiras de rodas e macas.

"Falta profissional suficiente aqui [...] Esse hospital atende mais de 10 bairros. Tem gente que chega aqui e ela mesma precisa pegar a maca ou a cadeira de rodas, isso quando tem. Hoje mais cedo tinha acompanhante pedindo uma maca e não tinha", desabafou.

A reportagem apurou que a Sesau vinha sendo cobrada para regularizar a documentação desde a última terça-feira. No entanto, as Ordens de Serviço só começaram a ser liberadas no sistema estadual por volta das 9h desta sexta , quando o trabalho começou a ser retomado.

Uma médica que atua no Pronto Atendimento Cosme e Silva por meio de empresa credenciada, e que não quis se identificar, explicou que apesar de terem sido liberadas, as novas Ordens de Serviço vieram com restrições na capacidade de atendimento .

"Foram liberadas [as Ordens de Serviço] parcialmente, com redução abrupta no número de plantões, o que, de qualquer maneira, vai impactar nos serviços ofertados à população. Muitos lugares ficarão desassistidos, já que só podemos cumprir a quantidade prevista pela Sesau [nas OSs]", disse a profissional.

O modelo de trabalho afetado pela falta de Ordem de Serviços faz parte de um projeto de credenciamento aberto do governo estadual. Nesse formato, o Estado contrata empresas para o fornecimento de profissionais de saúde em plantões de seis horas .

contratação serve para atuar de forma complementar ao Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS).

articles.title: Hospice Erasto Gaertner realiza cerimônia de memória em Curitiba | G1
articles.standfirst: Queima simbólica de mensagens deixadas por familiares ao longo do ano marcou celebração de espiritualidade, acolhimento e lembrança em Curitiba.
articles.summary: Queima simbólica de mensagens deixadas por familiares ao longo do ano marcou celebração de espiritualidade, acolhimento e lembrança em Curitiba.
articles.body:
O Hospice Erasto Gaertner realizou, em 31 de outubro de 2026, seu culto ecumênico, reunindo pacientes, familiares, colaboradores e convidados em uma manhã dedicada à espiritualidade, ao acolhimento e à homenagem. A celebração contou com a participação do Pastor Joceli e do Padre Elias, em um momento de reflexão e respeito às diferentes expressões de fé.

Um dos momentos centrais da cerimônia aconteceu junto à Oliveira do Hospice, onde foram queimadas simbolicamente as folhas nas quais familiares registraram mensagens e homenagens ao longo do ano. O gesto reuniu palavras, sentimentos e lembranças de pessoas que vivenciam a trajetória de cuidado na instituição.

A iniciativa integra as ações de acolhimento do Hospice Erasto Gaertner e representa uma oportunidade de reconhecer os vínculos construídos durante o cuidado, valorizando a memória e a história de cada família.

Foto: Divulgação/Hospital Erasto Gaertner.

A cerimônia realizada junto à Oliveira do Hospice tem como elemento central as mensagens deixadas por familiares ao longo do ano. Registradas em folhas, essas palavras são reunidas em um gesto simbólico de homenagem, reflexão e acolhimento.

A queima representa um momento coletivo para dar espaço às lembranças e aos sentimentos compartilhados por quem acompanha a trajetória de cuidado na instituição. A iniciativa também permite que familiares expressem suas experiências e mantenham vivas as memórias construídas ao lado de pessoas queridas.

O encontro integra a proposta de cuidado humanizado do Hospice, que considera as necessidades emocionais, afetivas e espirituais dos pacientes e de suas famílias.

Espiritualidade e acolhimento no cuidado paliativo

O culto ecumênico reuniu diferentes expressões religiosas e proporcionou um espaço de reflexão e participação, respeitando as crenças e a espiritualidade de cada pessoa.

No contexto dos cuidados paliativos, o acolhimento envolve diferentes dimensões da experiência humana. Além da assistência clínica, a atenção aos vínculos familiares, às necessidades emocionais e às questões espirituais pode fazer parte do cuidado oferecido a pacientes e familiares.

A participação do Pastor Joceli e do Padre Elias contribuiu para manter o caráter ecumênico da celebração, que reuniu a comunidade do Hospice em torno da memória, da fé e da valorização da vida.

O cuidado humanizado no Hospice Erasto Gaertner

A cerimônia faz parte de uma proposta de cuidado que reconhece a importância da dignidade, dos vínculos e da qualidade de vida em cada etapa da assistência.

Ao reunir pacientes, familiares e colaboradores, o culto ecumênico também valoriza a experiência compartilhada entre as pessoas que participam da rotina do Hospice. A iniciativa oferece um espaço de expressão e acolhimento para sentimentos que fazem parte da trajetória de pacientes e familiares.

O momento junto à Oliveira simboliza essa atenção às histórias individuais e às relações construídas durante o acompanhamento na instituição.

O Hospice Erasto Gaertner integra a Liga Paranaense de Combate ao Câncer e atua no cuidado de pacientes que necessitam de assistência paliativa. Sua proposta contempla o acolhimento de pacientes e familiares, com atenção ao conforto, à dignidade, à qualidade de vida e aos vínculos em cada etapa do cuidado.

articles.title: 'Papai Noel' humanoide estreia traje natalino no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Robô Tenório entrou em CTG de Estância Velha acompanhado de um 'cusco', também robô, com lenço no pescoço. Eles dançaram ao som de música gravada pelo cantor Rodrigo Silva em sua homenagem.
articles.summary: Robê Tenório entrou em CTG de Estância Velha acompanhado de um 'cusco', também robô, com lenço no pescoço. Eles dançaram ao som de música gravada em sua homenagem.
articles.body:
O robô “mais gaúcho do Brasil” estreou sua pilcha (traje típico gaúcho) natalina durante um evento beneficente realizado nesta quarta-feira (4), em Estância Velha , no Vale do Sinos.

O humanoide da Ultech School/Ulbra, entrou no CTG Gaudérios da Saudade vestido de Papai Noel e foi uma das atrações do jantar solidário em benefício do Hospital Municipal Getúlio Vargas, localizado no município.

Ele estava acompanhado de um "cusco", também robô, que usa um lenço no pescoço . Além de interagir com o público, o robô dançou ao som de “Tenório”, música gravada pelo cantor Rodrigo Silva em sua homenagem.

"Acredito que a tecnologia precisa estar conectada às pessoas, à cultura e à realidade em que vivemos. Ela não deve ser vista como algo que substitui a tradição, mas como uma ferramenta capaz de valorizá-la e aproximá-la das novas gerações", acredita Évelin Janner, diretora-executiva da Ultec School/Ulbra.

'Papai Noel humanoide', robô Tenório estreia traje natalino no RS — Foto: Giovani Grizotti/RBS TV

Sucesso no Mês Farroupilha ao vestir traje típico em visita ao Acampamento Farroupilha e estúdio do Jornal do Almoço, da RBS TV, Tenório não perdeu a desenvoltura, mesmo vestindo bombacha, camisa e lenço, algo que contrasta com os metais utilizados em sua fabricação.

"Preparamos o traje de modo a manter a mobilidade característica de um humanoide", diz Vânia Vargas, de Esteio , responsável por confeccionar a fantasia.

O evento foi promovido pela Associação Gaúcha Estanciense (AGE), que reúne quatro entidades tradicionalistas do município: CTG Gaudérios da Saudade, CTG Estância do Campo Grande, CTG Mourão da Estância e CTG Serigote. O encontro teve como atrações Os Monarcas, Hermanos Guedes e Projeto Taureando, além dos convidados especiais Paulo Dias Garcia e Wagner Schneider.

A programação também marcou a largada das inscrições para as Cavalgadas do Bem , mobilização que reúne cavaleiros e entidades tradicionalistas em uma grande corrente de solidariedade. A iniciativa da RBS TV e Rede Banco de Alimentos está marcada para o dia 12 de dezembro, com cavalgadas em todo o Rio Grande do Sul. O CTG também é ponto de coleta da campanha Natal do Bem.

articles.title: Vagas no Hospital Metropolitano de Ananindeua: veja detalhes | G1
articles.standfirst: São três cargos de níveis médio e superior, com uma vaga exclusiva para pessoa com deficiência. Prazos variam conforme a função, e a triagem é feita pelo RH.
articles.summary: O Hospital Metropolitano de Ananindeua oferece vagas de emprego para agente de portaria, auxiliar e analista, com prazos de inscrição até o dia 12 de novembro pelo RH.
articles.body:
Hospital Metropolitano de Urgência e Emergência (HMUE). — Foto: Pedro Guerreiro / Ag. Pará

O Hospital Metropolitano de Urgência e Emergência (HMUE), em Ananindeua , na Região Metropolitana de Belém, está com processos seletivos abertos para contratação de profissionais em áreas administrativas. As oportunidades são para agente de portaria, analista de folha de pagamento e auxiliar administrativo.

Os interessados devem atender aos requisitos específicos de cada função e fazer a inscrição dentro do prazo estabelecido para o cargo escolhido. Os links para inscrição estão logo abaixo.

Após o envio dos currículos, o setor de Recursos Humanos (RH) faz a triagem conforme os critérios de seleção. Os candidatos aprovados nessa etapa serão informados sobre datas, horários e locais das provas e entrevistas, quando houver.

Agente de portaria — exclusiva para Pessoas com Deficiência (PCD). Exige ensino médio completo; curso de agente de portaria e experiência na área são desejáveis. Inscrições até nove de novembro pelo link .

Auxiliar administrativo Núcleo Interno de Regulação (NIR) — apta a PCD. Exige ensino superior completo, conhecimento básico do pacote Office, experiência na área e disponibilidade total para a vaga. Inscrições até 11 de novembro pelo link .

Exige ensino superior completo em Contabilidade, Administração ou áreas afins, conhecimento intermediário do pacote Office, experiência no sistema Totvs e conhecimento no e-Social. Experiência na área é desejável. Inscrições até 12 de novembro pelo link .

articles.title: Motociclista de 36 anos morre após bater contra muro no Acre | G1
articles.standfirst: Jonas Silva Martins, de 36 anos, sofreu acidente na madrugada desta sexta-feira (6) em Cruzeiro do Sul. Ele trafegava em alta velocidade e havia consumido bebida alcoólica.
articles.summary: Jonas Silva Martins, de 36 anos, sofreu acidente na madrugada desta sexta-feira (6) em Cruzeiro do Sul. Ele trafegava em alta velocidade e havia consumido bebida alcoólica.
articles.body:
Jonas Silva Martins, de 36 anos morreu após perder o controle da moto e bater contra um muro na madrugada desta sexta-feira (6), em Cruzeiro do Sul — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O motociclista Jonas Silva Martins, de 36 anos, morreu após perder o controle da moto e bater contra um muro na madrugada desta sexta-feira (6), em Cruzeiro do Sul , interior do Acre.

O acidente aconteceu por volta das 2h, na Avenida 25 de Agosto, no bairro Aeroporto Velho, em frente à Empresa Brasileira de Pesquisa Agropecuária (Embrapa).

Ao g1 , a polícia Militar do Acre (PM-AC) informou que testemunhas relataram que Jonas seguia pela avenida no sentido bairro-centro, em alta velocidade, quando passou por uma faixa elevada de pedestres, perdeu o controle da motocicleta e saiu da pista.

Após a colisão, o motociclista caiu no chão, ao lado da moto. Pessoas que caminhavam pela região se aproximaram para prestar ajuda e acionaram o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu), que constatou a morte de Jonas ainda no local.

Ainda conforme os relatos reunidos pela PM, o motociclista havia passado momentos antes em uma residência no bairro Aeroporto Velho, onde consumiu bebida alcoólica.

Uma testemunha que também trabalhava com a vítima contou que se ofereceu para levá-la para casa, mas o homem recusou a carona e saiu pilotando a moto.

Essa testemunha afirmou ainda que seguiu atrás do colega para acompanhá-lo até a residência dele, no bairro do Telégrafo, e presenciou o acidente.

Segundo a PM, outras pessoas que estavam nas proximidades também tentaram ajudar a vítima antes da chegada do socorro.

O local foi isolado para o trabalho da perícia técnica. Após os procedimentos, o corpo foi recolhido pelo Instituto Médico Legal (IML).

A motocicleta foi removida ao pátio da 1ª Circunscrição Regional de Trânsito (Ciretran) porque estava com o licenciamento irregular.

articles.title: Lutador preso na Tijuca após agredir idosas em condomínio | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a polícia, Lucas Portela Fontana Gomes invadiu apartamentos e agrediu 2 vizinhas. Ele também foi baleado nas pernas durante a abordagem da PM. A Justiça decretou a prisão por tentativa de feminicídio.
articles.summary: O lutador Lucas Portela Fontana Gomes foi preso por tentativa de feminicídio após agredir idosas em um condomínio na Tijuca e ser baleado em ação da PM no Rio.
articles.body:
Um lutador de jiu-jítsu foi preso em flagrante após agredir pelo menos 2 vizinhas em um condomínio na Tijuca, Zona Norte do Rio de Janeiro , na madrugada desta quinta-feira (5). Um dos espancamentos foi gravado pela câmera de segurança do elevador (veja acima — as imagens são fortes) .

A Justiça converteu o flagrante em prisão preventiva por tentativa de feminicídio a pedido da 18ª DP (Praça da Bandeira).

Segundo os relatos reunidos na investigação, por volta da 1h Lucas Portela Fontana Gomes invadiu, sem motivo aparente , o apartamento de uma vizinha no 3º andar e agrediu uma idosa de 66 anos. Os parentes dela conseguiram deixar o imóvel e foram até a portaria pedir ajuda.

Uma vizinha do 2º andar, de 40 anos, ouviu os gritos e os pedidos de socorro e também desceu ao térreo. “Ele está com a minha avó!” , lhe disse um jovem.

Ela, então, subiu ao 3º pavimento para verificar o que estava acontecendo. Ao chegar, encontrou Lucas já na porta no elevador. Cachorros que estavam soltos no corredor entram na cabine.

Lucas Portela Fontana Gomes agride vizinha no elevador — Foto: Reprodução

Lucas, descalço e sem camisa, exige que a vizinha ajoelhe. Na sequência, dá um chute. “Você não me bate!” , pede a mulher.

O agressor ignora a súplica e inicia uma brutal sequência de socos e cotoveladas . A vítima, em vão, tenta se proteger com as mãos. O elevador desce ao térreo, mas ninguém aparece para ajudar .

As agressões continuam: Lucas encurrala a vizinha do elevador e passa a empurrar a cabeça dela contra uma parede . Depois, pelas costas, a estrangula com um “mata-leão” e a leva para o chão.

A mulher tem dificuldades para respirar. Lucas a solta, deitada no piso, e passa a socá-la no rosto , apoiando-se de joelhos no peito da vítima. Os cães tentam impedir as agressões.

O criminoso ainda a pega pelo pescoço e bate várias vezes a cabeça dela no chão . Lucas, então, sai do elevador e anda pela portaria, aos gritos.

Ensanguentada e com dificuldades para se levantar, a mulher sai do elevador, deixa o prédio e se abriga em um posto de gasolina próximo.

Pela manhã, policiais militares do 6º BPM (Tijuca) e agentes da Guarda Municipal foram chamados. Segundo o registro do caso, Lucas reagiu à abordagem e tentou pegar a arma de um policial.

Os PMs atiraram nas pernas dele. Ainda de acordo com o registro, mesmo ferido, Lucas resistiu à prisão e tentou subir pelas escadas. Ele foi imobilizado após o uso de uma arma de choque.

O caso é investigado pela 18ª DP. Lucas permanece preso e à disposição da Justiça.

As vítimas foram levadas para o Hospital Municipal Souza Aguiar. A idosa seguia internada com quadro estável, e mulher agredida no elevador teve alta.

articles.title: Prefeito de Barreiros acusa médicos de 'namorar' em hospital; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Carlinhos da Pedreira (PP) disse que viu profissionais durante visita surpresa. Prefeitura rescindiu contrato com associação que geria unidade e Cremepe repudiou exposição dos profissionais.
articles.summary: Carlinhos da Pedreira (PP) expulsou profissionais de unidade aos gritos e discussão viralizou nas redes sociais.
articles.body:
Uma discussão filmada dentro do hospital municipal de Barreiros , na Zona da Mata Sul de Pernambuco, viralizou nas redes sociais. As imagens mostram o prefeito Carlos Artur Soares de Avelar, conhecido como Carlinhos da Pedreira (PP), gritando com dois médicos e expulsando os profissionais do local durante uma visita surpresa (veja vídeo acima) .

No vídeo, o gestor diz que flagrou os trabalhadores "dormindo" e "namorando" no alojamento enquanto a emergência estava lotada. Após o ocorrido, a prefeitura anunciou a rescisão do contrato de gestão do Hospital Jailton Messias de Souza Albuquerque com a Associação João Paulo 2º.

O Conselho Regional de Medicina (Cremepe) repudiou a "exposição pública" dos plantonistas. Já o Sindicato dos Médicos de Pernambuco (Simepe) disse que a presença dos médicos, um homem e uma mulher, em ambiente de repouso não autoriza insinuações sobre sua vida íntima e que as imagens divulgadas não demonstram que eles estivessem "namorando" (saiba mais abaixo) .

O caso aconteceu na noite da quarta-feira (4). A "fiscalização surpresa" teria motivada por denúncias de falta de médicos na unidade. Nas imagens, o prefeito aparece percorrendo o hospital e começa a gritar com os médicos após entrar em uma das salas. Os nomes dos plantonistas não foram divulgados.

"Um absurdo o que vocês estão fazendo. Meus Deus do céu! A emergência lotada de gente e vocês aqui dormindo, namorando? É um absurdo. Vou botar para fora agora. Saiam daqui, desse hospital", gritou o prefeito. Logo em seguida, ele chama os profissionais de "vagabundos".

Em outro vídeo, publicado no perfil do prefeito também na quinta, Carlinhos da Pedreira afirmou, durante a participação em um podcast, que havia chegado do Recife por volta das 22h e decidiu entrar no hospital para verificar a unidade.

"Encontrei a recepção completamente lotada e perguntei: 'o que é que está acontecendo aqui no hospital?'. [Disseram]: 'tem três médicos, mas só tem um atendendo'. Eu comecei a procurar, bater em quarto a quarto, e encontrei dois médicos, no mesmo quarto, dormindo, e a população deixando de ser atendida. Disse que eu não admitia aquilo, que era um absurdo o que eles estavam fazendo, que era uma negligência médica, demiti eles na hora", disse.

O g1 procurou a Associação João Paulo II para se manifestar sobre a fiscalização feita pelo prefeito e a rescisão do contrato, mas não obteve resposta até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Por meio de nota, a prefeitura de Barreiros informou que a Secretaria de Saúde reassumirá diretamente a gestão administrativa, operacional e assistencial do hospital. Segundo a gestão municipal, a medida é temporária e já deu início ao processo licitatório para contratar uma nova organização que assuma a administração da unidade.

O município disse, ainda, que decidiu rescindir o contrato de gestão nº 026/2024 após o acompanhamento e a avaliação da execução contratual, "considerando os princípios da legalidade, da responsabilidade administrativa e do interesse público". Ainda de acordo com a gestão:

a prefeitura reconhece e agradece à Associação João Paulo II pelos serviços prestados durante o período de parceria;

está adotando as medidas administrativas necessárias para garantir uma transição organizada;

considera a continuidade dos atendimentos, a qualidade da assistência e o bem-estar dos usuários do Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) prioridades.

Por meio de nota, o Cremepe disse que repudia a exposição dos médicos plantonistas e que questionamentos sobre a assistência médica, escalas de plantão e funcionamento dos serviços de saúde devem ser tratados pelos meios institucionais e legais competentes, "sem constrangimento dos profissionais envolvidos".

"A fiscalização dos serviços públicos de saúde não confere a qualquer gestor o direito de expor médicos ao julgamento público, tampouco de comprometer sua honra, imagem e dignidade profissional. Esses direitos devem ser respeitados independentemente da existência de denúncias ou questionamentos sobre a atuação dos profissionais", afirmou a entidade no texto.

Já o Sindicato dos Médicos de Pernambuco (Simepe) afirmou que:

"repudia veementemente a abordagem do prefeito de Barreiros", marcada por constrangimento público e insinuações sobre a vida íntima dos profissionais;

fiscalizar os serviços públicos é dever da gestão, mas "humilhar trabalhadores, antecipar julgamentos e alimentar sua exposição ao descrédito são condutas incompatíveis com a responsabilidade do cargo";

a presença de uma médica e um médico em ambiente de repouso não autoriza insinuações de natureza íntima e as imagens divulgadas não demonstram o comportamento insinuado;

também repudia qualquer tentativa de desqualificação profissional "apoiada em estereótipos de gênero e no julgamento da vida privada de mulheres";

recebeu relatos de que os profissionais estavam em momento de descanso depois de uma intensa atividade assistencial nas primeiras 12 horas de plantão enquanto um terceiro médico continuava atendendo;

o repouso durante os plantões deve ser organizado com garantia de continuidade dos atendimentos e sua utilização não configura, por si só, abandono do serviço.

articles.title: Doação de órgãos em Volta Redonda: profissionais fazem homenagem | G1
articles.standfirst: Homenagem aconteceu em um hospital particular após captação de coração, rins, fígado, córneas e tecido musculoesquelético. Família autorizou a doação.
articles.summary: A doação de órgãos em Volta Redonda mobilizou equipes de saúde em um corredor de aplausos após a captação de coração, rins e fígado para pacientes em espera.
articles.body:
Profissionais de um hospital particular de Volta Redonda (RJ) formaram um corredor de aplausos em homenagem a uma doadora de órgãos e à família dela na quarta-feira (4).

O gesto aconteceu após a captação de órgãos e tecidos da paciente, que teve a morte encefálica confirmada.

Segundo o hospital, a família autorizou a doação e foram captados coração, rins, fígado, córneas e tecido musculoesquelético. Este foi o terceiro processo de doação de órgãos realizado na unidade.

Profissionais fazem corredor de aplausos em homenagem a doadora de órgãos em Volta Redonda — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

O procedimento foi conduzido pela Comissão Intra-Hospitalar de Doação de Órgãos e Tecidos para Transplante (CIHDOTT), em conjunto com a Central Estadual de Transplantes do Rio de Janeiro, responsável pela destinação dos órgãos aos pacientes da fila de espera.

Coração captado em Volta Redonda é levado de helicóptero a Resende para seguir ao Paraná

Um coração captado em um hospital de Volta Redonda (RJ) foi transportado de helicóptero até Resende (RJ), nesta quarta-feira (4), para seguir viagem ao Paraná. O deslocamento entre as duas cidades do Sul do Rio durou 20 minutos.

A operação foi realizada pela Superintendência de Operações Aéreas (SOAer), da Secretaria de Estado de Saúde do Rio de Janeiro, em parceria com a Casa Civil do Paraná.

Segundo a secretaria, a captação foi concluída às 13h40. O órgão foi levado pela equipe do helicóptero Saúde 02 até Resende, onde uma aeronave da Casa Civil do Paraná aguardava para continuar o transporte.

articles.title: Phone First: Northern Ireland health trusts told to 'pause' plans to cut service
articles.summary: The triage line was scrapped in Belfast and was to close in the Northern Trust later this month.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland's health minister has instructed trusts which have not yet stood down their Phone First service to "pause any planned cessation" of the scheme.

The telephone triage system has already been scrapped by the Belfast Trust; it was to end within weeks in the Northern Trust and is under review in the Western Trust.

Phone First is aimed at reducing unnecessary visits to hospital emergency departments (EDs) by providing advice to patients on appropriate care options.

In a statement to BBC News NI, the Department of Health (DoH) said health trusts that have not yet stood the service down will be "liaising with their external providers for an extension".

The Northern Trust's line was due to close on 27 November, but its interim chief executive, Suzanne Pullins said on Thursday that they have been told to "pause the formal withdrawal to allow for reassessment".

Pullins announced the development as she appeared before Stormont's Health Committee to answer questions about the trust's savings plans.

NI emergency departments to trial phone triage

Lagan Valley ED introduces 'phone first' service

GP telephone first system 'here to stay'

Last month, committee members had expressed concern that Phone First was being cut just as hospital EDs prepared to deal with increased winter pressures.

Pullins acknowledged those concerns on Thursday, saying the decision to stand it down was in "no way a reflection of the service" which was "very valued".

But she explained that there were "no easy choices" given the scale of the financial savings the trust had been asked to find.

Phone First costs £500,000 to run and the trust has been asked to make £53.8m in savings for this year.

The DoH statement said that the Belfast Trust had redeployed its Phone First staff "to urgent care services to secure access to Urgent and Emergency Care".

It added that all trusts are focused on supporting EDs "to ensure optimal patient flow and access to the right care in the right place at the right time and from the right clinician to meet the patient needs".

Phone First was initially introduced during the pandemic in late 2020 to reduce the risk of Covid-19 spreading among patients in crowded hospital waiting rooms.

Under the system, patients call a dedicate line before travelling to hospital to check if they really need to go to an ED or if they could be treated elsewhere

Operating in a similar manner the NHS's non-emergency 111 medical helpline in England, Scotland and Wales, it was designed to be used in urgent but not life-threatening cases - the public is still advised to always call 999 immediately if someone's life is at risk.

It was trialled in Causeway Hospital before being gradually rolled out across all five hospital trust areas.

However, it was run by five separate teams who each had different hours and different contact numbers.

Before it closed its line at the end of September, the Belfast Trust estimated that move would save it approximately £500,000.

At last month's health committee meeting, senior staff from the Belfast Trust were questioned about their decision to cut the line as winter approached.

"It's frustrating, it's not something that we wanted to do... but we felt that it was the least worst option," said Claire Corry, Director of Finance at the Belfast Trust.

Her boss, Chief Executive Jennifer Welsh, explained the projected £800m shortfall in Northern Ireland's health budget meant all trusts had been instructed to find savings that "could be delivered without causing harm to service users".

Welsh explained Phone First was scrapped in Belfast in order to prioritise other services that "we think would generate more benefit for patients and staff".

She told Northern Ireland Assembly members at the 22 October meeting that there "wasn't a huge uptake in the service" and that it "wasn't having a huge impact".

However, Northern Ireland-wide statistics show a rising trend in usage over the past six years.

The Belfast Telegraph reported that calls reached their highest ever level in the same month that Belfast Trust closed its line.

Phone First Calls (October 2020 - September 2026)

There were 18,263 calls in September, 12,098 (66%) of which resulted in patients being referred on to EDs.

It was suggested to last month's committee that because two thirds of callers end up in EDs anyway, Phone First was less effective than some other services at reducing pressures.

But committee chair Philip McGuigan, of Sinn Féin, pointed out that Phone First may have helped to keep more than 6,000 callers out of ED in September alone.

During that meeting, McGuigan secured the support of the committee to write to the DoH to ask about the future of Phone First.

Before the minister announced the pause, BBC News NI had contacted all five trusts this week to ask about the future of their telephone triage services.

The Belfast Trust said its decision to stop its Phone First was taken "in the context of the very significant financial challenge" it and the wider health service was facing.

It added "other care options are still available" and pointed patients to its Choose the Right Care webpage in cases of urgent but non-life-threatening illness or injury.

The Western Trust said its Phone First service was being "assessed against current spend and affordability" as part of its savings plan.

"No decision has been made at this time and the service continues to operate as normal," its spokesperson added.

The South Eastern Trust said its Phone First service at both the Lagan Valley and Downe hospitals "will remain unchanged".

It added that Phone First is "not required" at the Ulster Hospital because its Urgent Care Centre directs patients "to the most appropriate service when they arrive".

A spokesman for the Southern Trust told BBC News NI it has no plans to withdraw Phone First.

articles.title: Wisconsin infant dies of measles as state sees first death from disease since 1990
articles.summary: Wisconsin's health officials announced an infant's measles-associated death, marking the state's first in 36 years, amid 431 cases in 13 counties.
articles.body: An infant in Wisconsin died of measles, marking the state’s first death linked to the disease in 36 years, the state's Department of Health Services announced on Thursday. The Department of Health Services said the child died in southwestern Wisconsin but did not provide a more precise location. The department said it would not release any additional details to protect the privacy of the family. The coroner listed the immediate cause of death as measles. "It is with a heavy heart we are reporting the first death of an infant connected with a measles outbreak in Wisconsin in many years. My heart is broken for the family," state Department of Health Services Secretary Kirsten Johnson said in a statement. CHILD'S MEASLES DEATH MARKS NEW YORK STATE'S FIRST IN MORE THAN 30 YEARS AMID OUTBREAK "Any death of a child is a tragedy and even more so when it is related to a vaccine-preventable disease. Measles can cause serious illness and death, and it is important for all Wisconsinites to evaluate their risk and take steps to protect themselves and their family," she continued. Measles can cause life-threatening complications, including pneumonia and swelling of the brain. The department said that while anyone can become seriously ill, children younger than 5, pregnant people and people with weakened immune systems are at increased risk of complications. Wisconsin has reported 431 measles cases in 13 counties so far this year, reflecting the highest number of cases seen in the state in more than 35 years. Among these cases, nine people required hospitalization for severe symptoms. State officials urged Wisconsinites to be proactive in preventing illness to protect themselves and their communities, saying the best way to prevent measles is with the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services previously told FOX News Digital that "Secretary Kennedy and CDC Director Dr. Erica Schwartz continue to make clear that the MMR vaccine is the most effective way to prevent measles." Earlier this week, a child in New York state's Lewis County died in the first known measles-associated death in the state in more than 30 years. New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said she was "heartbroken" to learn of the child's death. "As a mother and grandmother, I cannot imagine what this family is going through. My heart goes out to everyone who knew and loved this child," Hochul said in a statement. NEW YORK DECLARES MEASLES DISASTER EMERGENCY AS CASES SURGE IN PENNSYLVANIA CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has reported four measles-associated deaths across the country this year, although state health departments have reported higher figures. In Pennsylvania, state health officials have confirmed six measles-associated deaths in 2026 and are investigating another reported death that has not yet met the state's criteria to be classified as measles-associated. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Teen with cerebral palsy finds escape in music and TV dream
articles.summary: Music helps Izzy escape daily pain as the teen prepares to perform with the BBC Children in Need choir.
articles.body:
"Music takes me to a different place," says a teenager with cerebral palsy who has landed the chance to perform on national television.

Some days 14-year-old Izzy struggles to get around because of pain caused by his condition. But when he picks up a guitar or starts singing, he says he can escape into another world.

Known by friends and family as "the happiest person in the world", Izzy, from West Lavington in Wiltshire, has been selected to perform in the 2026 BBC Children in Need Choir.

"It's really exciting, a once-in-a-lifetime experience to do something that special," he said.

'Flawed' training contributed to officer's death

Rape-accused tells jury woman 'participated' and did not appear drugged

Veterans march to highlight 'unseen scars' of PTSD

Despite living with cerebral palsy and a spinal condition that can leave him fatigued and in pain, Izzy rarely stops smiling.

"Music takes me to a different place, into how the music is described and the places they are - that's where I'm escaping to," he said.

His mum, Rachael, said: "He just loves life and makes the best of everything. He likes to talk, to be involved, to help."

The choir will perform on the national Children in Need broadcast on 13 November, an opportunity Rachael described as a "crazy dream" come true.

Izzy was born nine weeks premature, and spent the first month of his life at Salisbury District Hospital.

Early on, his family noticed he wasn't developing as quickly as other babies - he couldn't sit, crawl or walk - and was eventually diagnosed with cerebral palsy aged two and a half.

"I also have a spinal problem where my bones rub together, which isn't the most comfy," explained Izzy.

"It can affect my daily life. One day I may be able to get around, the next I can't. Sometimes I feel uncomfortable and in pain," he said.

Izzy - who was named after Isambard Kingdom Brunel - walks with splints on his lower legs to help with balance.

"Yes it's true, I'm known for always smiling. I do things that are happy. I think it makes other people feel better too," he said.

Izzy has started volunteering to help younger children at the West Lavington Youth Club (WLYC), where he's been going for five years.

The club has received money from Children In Need in the past.

"He brings a load of energy to the group, even though he has physical disabilities it doesn't hold him back," said Josh Newton, the manager of WLYC.

"He doesn't need to be asked to help, he just does."

The choir will perform a mash up of 'Stargazing' by Myles Smith and the Candi Staton classic 'You Got The Love' as part of the national CiN show.

"It'll mean everything to him," said Rachael.

"He's just blown away by it. It's like a crazy, crazy dream"

articles.title: Rosalía, cantante, sobre su relación con sus seres queridos: "La soledad es mi lección de vida"
articles.standfirst: La española es reacia a estar o sentirse sola
articles.summary: La española es reacia a estar o sentirse sola
articles.body: Muchos nos hemos visto obligados a estar en algún momento de nuestra vida en soledad. Este es un estado en el que muchos no quieren estar y rechazan por completo. Eso es algo que le sucede a la artista española Rosalía, quien acaba de ser nombrada con el Premio Ondas a Fenómeno Musical del Año, mencionó en una entrevista realizada por Ana Millán, en el primer episodio de 'Ex. La vida después'; que no le gusta la soledad; "soy muy sociable, me gusta estar rodeada de mis amigos, de mi familia. Me encanta tener pareja y me gusta el afecto." La soledad no es mala de por sí, pero tal y como mencionó la artista, Rosalía mencionó en dicha entrevista algunas de sus estrategias para eludir la soledad. Los expertos mencionan algunos consejos además si no estamos preparados para encontrarnos con nosotros mismos. Una de las estrategias para incorporar en nuestro día a día si no somos amigos de la soledad, los expertos recomiendan que te involucres en grupos y actividades comunitarias, así como talleres, clubs de lectura o grupos de senderismo, entre muchos ejemplos. Involucrarte en voluntariados puede ser otra opción muy positiva que, además, te llene. Además, puede ser una idea muy positiva cultivar tus vínculos cercanos, retomando el contacto con tus amigos y familiares a través de llamadas, cartas o redes sociales. Mantén tu red social abierta y procura ser amable con tus seres queridos para mantenerte al día con ellos. No solo debemos intentar eludir la soledad, muchas veces, debemos llegar a mejorar otros aspectos para poder aceptarla cuando esta nos llegue porque, es inevitable, que en algún momento de nuestras vidas la experimentemos. Para afrontarla con seguridad y con confianza, debemos cuidar el bienestar físico y mental a través de hábitos como la práctica de ejercicio de forma regular, una higiene de sueño saludable y destinar algo de tiempo a la meditación y el autodiálogo positivo. Por último, es importante que también seamos capaces de aprender a disfrutar de nuestra propia compañía, transformando nuestro espacio en ese refugio agradable y apacible en el que se puedan realizar actividades individuales que nos generen pasión. Sobre todo, es importante que cuando la soledad llegue y nos arrolle, sepamos encontrar el apoyo profesional para que la sensación de vacío o de aislamiento nos duela, haga daño o perturbe. La soledad no es mala aunque, encajarla, pueda ser complejo en muchas ocasiones de nuestras vidas.

articles.title: Leiva, cantante y cómo gestiona su salud mental: “He aprendido a convivir con el bicho de la ansiedad”
articles.standfirst: Así lo mencionó en un reportaje publicado en ‘EL PAÍS Semanal’
articles.summary: Así lo mencionó en un reportaje publicado en ‘EL PAÍS Semanal’
articles.body: Leiva, el cantante y artista español, ha recibido el Premio Ondas 2026 a la Trayectoria Musical; un premio que reconoce la gran carrera artística que ha tenido desde el momento en el que empezó. Sin embargo, tal y como se mencionaba en un reportaje en el ‘EL PAÍS Semanal’ publicado en el año 2025; en el que el propio artista mencionada que ha aprendido "a convivir con el bicho de la ansiedad” en relación a los ataques de pánico y a cómo intenta gestionarlos pese al paso de los años y acostumbrarse a los escenarios, la música y todo lo que conlleva. Aunque pueda parecer una respuesta sorprendente, la realidad es que sí podemos y debemos aprender a convivir con la ansiedad, pero no como una resignación al sufrimiento, sino como lo que es: una regulación y respuesta natural del cuerpo ante un evento concreto. Las claves para entender este proceso es ver la ansiedad como una alarma y no como un enemigo, ya que es un mecanismo ideal del cuerpo para gestionar la incertidumbre o el peligro. Uno de nuestros errores es intentar erradicarlo cuando debemos aprender a gestionarla a través de la ayuda de un profesional. Por ese motivo es necesario que se deje de evitar y que no se huya de lo que te genera ansiedad, cuando lo que debemos es exponernos de forma gradual para ayudar a que pierda fuerza poco a poco eso que tanto nos aterra. Siempre que lo necesites es recomendable que busques apoyo profesional para ayudarte a gestionar estas situaciones. Gestionar la ansiedad es posible en varias dimensiones. En la relativa al nivel corporal se pueden bajar las revoluciones físicas a través de la respiración diafragmática, la relajación muscular progresiva y el anclaje al presente cuando sientas que estás perdiendo el control. Por otro lado, está el nivel mental que debe tratarse a través del cuestionamiento del pensamiento preguntándonos de forma objetiva qué es lo que nos sucede y por qué nos surge este pensamiento en un primer momento. Debemos empezar por aceptar de forma radical en lugar de luchar contra la sensación buscando la calma y el descarte de los nervios. Además, es importante que se distinga entre la preocupación útil e inútil para ver si el problema tiene una solución en la actualidad. Por último, debemos cuidar también el nivel conductual, ya que tus hábitos son importantes evitando la evitación e intentando no huir de una situación que te genere ansiedad. Además, debemos tener en nuestra vida diaria una serie de hábitos reguladores para quemar el exceso de cortisol y la adrenalina.
